gen_risks.description: Geopolitical volatility in the MENA region creates economic instability and heightens risk exposure for private investors and startups.
gen_risks.mitigation: Co-invest alongside established international and GCC venture capital funds to de-risk equity investments and diversify sector exposure.
gen_risks.evidence: Jordan’s small, open economy continues to face vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region.

gen_risks.description: High-growth Jordanian startups may relocate headquarters to GCC or US markets due to larger market sizes and abundant long-term capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate explicit side-letter covenants requiring portfolio funds and startups to maintain core business operations and technical staffing in Jordan.
gen_risks.evidence: Availability of long-term funding and market size in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, US and other markets prompt high-growth Jordanian startups to expand elsewhere

gen_risks.description: Underdeveloped financial sector instruments and reliance on conservative commercial banking limit early-stage equity financing availability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy ISSF 2.0 public capital through a catalytic Fund of Funds model and targeted co-investments to mobilize early-stage venture capital.
gen_risks.evidence: underscored challenges such as underdeveloped financial instruments and reliance on traditional banking system with a subdued credit growth.

gen_risks.description: Historical management and technical team turnover at ISSF could recur and impair capital deployment efficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain competitive market-aligned staff compensation, institutionalize team retention strategies, and streamline governance oversight structures.
gen_risks.evidence: In the initial years of operation, ISSF faced challenges linked to, for example, high turnover of the team.

gen_risks.description: Overexposure of capital to individual venture capital funds presents portfolio concentration risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish strict nominal exposure caps and percentage limits on single fund investments within the Project Operations Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate and manage concentration risks, the current ISSF Investment Strategy sets out the limit on ISSF investment in one VC fund.

gen_risks.description: Underlying VC fund managers or startups may engage in financial mismanagement, fraud, or operational non-compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Institutionalize mandatory Operational Due Diligence (ODD) checks and continuous oversight monitoring for all portfolio fund managers.
gen_risks.evidence: ensuring that underlying funds follow robust operational practices and have the tools and capacity to monitor risks such as fraud, mismanagement, or regulatory non-compliance.

gen_risks.description: ISSF PMU and financial intermediaries may lack sufficient technical capacity to manage World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESS).
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire dedicated Environmental and Social specialists and mandate that all participating VC funds establish compliant Environmental and Social Management Systems.
gen_risks.evidence: ISSF 1.0 was prepared under the previous World Bank safeguards... hence, ISSF requires improved E&S risks and impacts management capacity

gen_risks.description: Expanded SME and tech startup operations may generate hazardous e-waste, creating environmental pollution and worker health risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed environmental screening criteria and mandatory e-waste recycling management clauses into sub-project investment legal agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: SMEs’ supported activities may cause environmental impacts connected to mismanagement of e-waste, including pollution, Occupational Health and Safety

gen_risks.description: Gaps between national labor legislation and World Bank ESS2 standards create risks regarding worker non-discrimination and contractor oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement specific labor gap-filling measures in the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) to complement Jordanian Labor Law.
gen_risks.evidence: There are gaps with ESS2 in the following areas: lack of non-discrimination provisions based on gender, disability and citizenship; worker’s organizations

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder accessibility to the Grievance Mechanism (GM) may prevent affected parties from lodging operational complaints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade the ISSF GM procedures, enhance uptake channels, and establish confidential, survivor-centered resolution pathways for SEA/SH complaints.
gen_risks.evidence: according to a recent E&S audit for ISSF, it was found that the GM system requires enhancement to ensure that all affected parties

gen_risks.description: Decreased precipitation, extreme heat events, and water scarcity present climate risks to domestic business continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target 10 percent of project investment capital towards greentech and climate-resilient solutions across Fund of Funds and co-investment components.
gen_risks.evidence: expected decrease in total precipitation, with increased variability in the location, timing, and quantity of rainfall; increased drought occurrence

gen_risks.description: Incomplete implementation tools under the national public procurement bylaw create procedural uncertainty for project procurement activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated procurement specialist at ISSF PMU and apply standardized private sector Commercial Practices accepted by the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: enactment of the public procurement bylaw has brought significant improvement... several of the implementation tools are under development

gen_risks.description: Delays in fulfilling mandatory effectiveness conditions could postpone loan effectiveness and subsequent capital deployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactively finalize the Subsidiary Agreement, Project Operations Manual, Corporate Governance Manual, and Articles of Association prior to loan signing.
gen_risks.evidence: The Borrower has adopted, and caused ISSF to adopt, the Project Operations Manual, in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.

gen_risks.description: Supported ICT startups may face data privacy and cybersecurity vulnerabilities during digital service scaling.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include data privacy and technical security standards within the screening criteria and operational due diligence for sub-project investments.
gen_risks.evidence: the proposed Project could entail social risks, including poor labor and working conditions, limited stakeholder engagement, the digital divide, data privacy and security risks

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. External economic shocks, regional instability and related uncertainties, or a downturn in global venture capital markets could reduce investor confidence and slow private capital mobilization. Additionally, Jordan's nascent venture capital market and competition from more developed ecosystems in neighboring countries may impact startup retention and funding.

Other risks are rated Substantial and relate to geopolitical risk. Jordan's strategic location makes it susceptible to a complex set of geopolitical challenges that have intensified in recent years, due to the current Conflict in the Middle East and its repercussions for investment, trade, and tourism in the region. Increasing geopolitical risks may prompt adjustments in policy and budgetary priorities and/or contribute to delays in implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: By combining regional and global diplomacy, building international partnerships, staying the course on political and economic modernization reforms, implementing prudent fiscal policies, and strategic security measures, Jordan has maintained its resilience and stability despite continuous crises.
